title: I couldn't render an infinite mirror, so I let it reflect only once. It was a lie, but it looked like a mirror, and that became the whole game
author: office-canard
selftext:
UNMIRROR started with mirror reflection. I wanted to do something with bouncing angles, and for a couple of days it was going to be a sport, something like squash.



Then I built a white room with mirrors on all four sides and ran into a problem. A real mirrored room reflects forever, the tunnel of copies going back into the dark. I couldn't render that, so I let the reflection happen exactly once and stopped.



That's a lie. Anyone who has stood between two mirrors knows it. But on screen it didn't read as a lie at all. It read as a mirror.



That interested me more than squash. If a mirror can be that wrong and still be believed, how much further can it be wrong? What if the thing standing in front of it doesn't show up in it at all?



Mirrors are uncomfortable objects. They show up in horror everywhere, and not by accident. So I followed the discomfort instead of the ball.



I put a door in the room. You go through it, and you're in the same room again. Almost. Each time, something is slightly off, and you have to find what changed to get out. Most of what I put in there I'd rather not describe, because finding it is the game. But here's one: at a certain point, the sound of your own footsteps changes. I expected it to be a small detail. It wasn't. You don't feel that something happened to you. You feel that you've changed.



How AI fit in: verification, mostly. The game ships with 939 assertions across 27 harnesses, run headless before anything reaches a browser, including 44 cases that have to fail when I break them on purpose. I'm one person. I would have stopped caring by the third pass.



And Claude forgets everything between sessions, so the project grew a handoff document, eleven versions of it now, whose first section is nothing but rules learned from things that went wrong. Don't build for a case that can't happen. Don't claim a spec without measuring it. It's the most useful file in the project, and it only exists because my collaborator resets.
